text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a ~30% p95 latency regression on SSE streaming endpoints after last rollout (feature/stream-encode v3). Small responses (<=200 tokens) hit worst. Canaries bright red.
alan: Ugh. Any quick repro or logs?
maria: Repro locally on canary cluster. Minimal curl test: 
```
# quick local repro
time curl -s -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://canary.api.redwood/stream?model=x'
# first byte ~35ms, whole response p95 ~120ms vs baseline ~90ms
```
jia: Perf CI also flagged this morning: streaming-latency job failed, +25% p95 vs baseline. See job: https://ci.redwood/jobs/streaming-latency/7845 :eyes:
deploy-bot: Rollout of release/stream-encode-v3 paused (canary thresholds breached).
ken: My guess: the new framing/encoding path added extra toolcall header marshalling that forces buffer flushes. Could be interacting with batching heuristics and kernel autoselect decisions.
maria: Interesting — small responses look serialized (encode step) rather than token generation. Jia, can you run a CPU profile on the encoder?
jia: Ran pprof on canary. Hot traces: 
```
- ProtoEncoder::encode_tool_call 42%
- SSEWriter::flush_frame 18%
- KernelAutoSelect::score 8%
- KVCache::evict_if_needed 6%
```
jia: ProtoEncoder is doing a few extra copies for tool metadata now (string joins + base64). That explains extra CPU on small payloads.
alan: Could KV eviction be making batching worse? If framing increases per-request size it might trigger different batching windows and kernel choices.
ken: I instrumented batching window on canary — average batch size down 12% for short requests after v3, likely due to earlier flushes. Kernel autoselect then picks a lower-efficiency kernel for the smaller batch distribution. Chain reaction.
nate: Reproduced locally with unit test that simulates many small toolcall responses. Patch candidate: avoid eager frame flush on tool metadata if SSE chunk is small; coalesce metadata into main payload.
perf-ci: Perf job details: baseline p95=88ms, current p95=112ms, top diff at encoder stage. Attachments: perf flame and raw profiles in job artifacts.
sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026 for customer impact on streaming. Not paging yet but tracking.
maria: Thanks. Quick mitigation plan: 1) open hotfix to revert the framing change that does eager metadata flush (PR #6251), 2) run a targeted canary with perf probes, 3) follow-up: rewrite ProtoEncoder to avoid extra copies + add a microbenchmark.
ken: I'll take the bisect range: commits between c3f9d1..a8b7c2 look suspect. Starting narrow-down now.
alan: If bisect points to the encoder change, we should revert and ship hotfix today. Otherwise fallback to reverting kernel-autoselect tweaks we rolled together.
jia: Also saw elevated KV cache churn during the canary — eviction spikes correlate with the time when batch size drops. Possible that smaller batches increase KV locality misses. Will add KV metrics to perf probes.
maria: Cool. If hotfix/revert lands, I'll rerun canary perf and report numbers. Please add short notes to the incident.
deploy-bot: PR #6251 (revert: stream-encode-v3 framing) merged to release candidate. Deploying to canary.
alan: Can someone run the microbench script against canary after deploy? `scripts/perf/streaming_microbench --small-requests`
nate: Ran it post-revert: p95 back to ~90ms for small responses. Improvement visible in perf CI artifacts. :thumbsup:
maria: Nice — rolling out rollback to wider canary. Ken, continue bisect to get permanent fix. Jia, KV follow-up. Alan, add regression test to CI to catch encoder regressions on small responses.
ken: Will open a tracking issue with the bisect results and a proposed encoder patch.
jia: Filing KV cache follow-up ticket too.
maria: Closing loop: short-term rollback mitigated customer impact. Longer-term: optimize ProtoEncoder + add coalescing + add perf regression gates. Thanks team. :shipit:
